=== CALL C0467 ===
Nadeesha: Hello! Hi, can you hear me okay? Sorry, my screen froze for a second there.
Hannah: Hiya, yeah, I can hear you fine. I'm Hannah. I'm in Norwich.
Nadeesha: Lovely. I'm Nadeesha, I'm in Cardiff. Sorry, I'm always a bit nervous with these video things, you know, in case something goes wrong.
Hannah: Oh, same. I was convinced my laptop was going to die during that puzzle bit. Did you finish it?
Nadeesha: Erm, mostly? I got stuck on the last one, actually. I kept thinking there was a trick. How about you?
Hannah: No, I ran out of time. I'm rubbish at that sort of thing under pressure. Give me an essay and I'm fine.
Nadeesha: An essay? Are you studying?
Hannah: Yeah, part-time with the Open University, Arts and Humanities. I'm in my third year. I do it in the evenings once my daughter's in bed, so it's a lot of late nights and cups of tea. In the day I'm a senior midday supervisor at a primary school, so lunchtimes, the playground, all the fallouts. And I do breakfast club as well, which is honestly my favourite bit.
Nadeesha: Oh, that's lovely. That's a lot, actually, with a little one. How old is she?
Hannah: Isla's nine. She's obsessed with drawing horses at the moment, just horses, on everything.
Nadeesha: Aw. My daughter is eight, Sanuli. With her it's swimming. Tuesdays are swimming lessons, so Tuesdays are a nightmare for me, sorry, not a nightmare, just very rushed.
Hannah: No, nightmare's fair, I get it. What do you do, then?
Nadeesha: I'm a senior procurement officer for one of the health boards here, so NHS. Basically I manage the tenders and the supplier contracts for medical consumables, gloves, dressings, syringes, that sort of thing. It sounds boring, but actually it's quite a lot of negotiating, and I like that part. I like being the one in the meeting who has actually read the contract, you know?
Hannah: Ha, that's a good skill. I bet the suppliers hate you.
Nadeesha: Some of them, maybe! This week was all supplier meetings, so I'm knackered, honestly. Is that the right word, knackered?
Hannah: That's exactly the right word. I'm knackered most Fridays. Chips Friday at school is chaos, the queue goes round the hall.
Nadeesha: I can imagine. And what do you want to do with the degree? Sorry, is that too nosy?
Hannah: No, not at all. I'd love to go into museum learning, like running school workshops at Norwich Castle or somewhere like that. I volunteered at a half-term family day and absolutely loved it. It's taken me a while to get here, I left uni at nineteen because I was skint, so this is sort of round two.
Nadeesha: That's really nice, actually. I think it's good to do it when you really want it, no?
Hannah: Yeah, I hope so. Fingers crossed. Do you get to travel much, with work and Sanuli?
Nadeesha: Erm, we go back to Sri Lanka every other year, for a month. My family is in Kandy. And we try to do a city break. Last year was Lisbon, which was beautiful. We stayed in a really nice hotel near the river.
Hannah: Oh, I'd love Lisbon. My dream is Florence, to see the actual frescoes. I've got a little savings jar for it. Very slowly.
Nadeesha: You should go! Florence is meant to be amazing. Erm, sorry, I don't know much about frescoes, actually. Are they the paintings on the walls?
Hannah: Yeah, painted straight onto wet plaster. My course has me looking at medieval wall paintings, so I've gone a bit nerdy about it.
Nadeesha: No, that's interesting. Sanuli would like that, she loves painting. Is that okay, sorry, I keep talking about my daughter.
Hannah: Don't be daft, I've been going on about horses! Does she draw as well, or is it more...

Hardik: Yeah.

Hardik: Yeah, I can imagine you'd need that.
Gemma: You do. So is it just you looking after her then, full-time?
Hardik: Mostly. She goes to her mum's in Leicester some weekends and holidays. My mum helps as well, she lives ten minutes away. She sends me back with way too much food every week, theplas, curries, everything.
Gemma: Oh, that's nice though, isn't it? I wish my mum did that. She's just had her knee done, so it's the other way round at the moment, I'm sort of running round after her.
Hardik: Sorry to hear that. Is she alright?
Gemma: Yeah, she's getting there, thanks. It just makes you realise, you know? Anyway, do you get much time to yourself, with work and everything?
Hardik: Not really. After she's in bed I play a bit of FIFA, watch the cricket highlights. India lost the last one, so that was a bad night, innit.
Gemma: Oh no! I couldn't tell you a single cricket player, sorry. My husband's more into football. Do you ever get to...

=== CALL C0469 ===
Hannah: Hiya! Can you hear me alright?
Tomasz: Yes, I can hear you. I am Tomasz. I'm in Reading.
Hannah: I'm Hannah, Norwich. Nice to meet you. How did you find the puzzle thing at the start?
Tomasz: It was fine. I finished with about one minute left.
Hannah: Oh, show-off! I ran out of time completely. So what do you do, Tomasz?
Tomasz: I am a student. Construction Management at University of Reading, second year. Before that I worked six years at a distribution warehouse near Theale, shift team leader. I still do some weekend shifts there in summer.
Hannah: Oh, that's brilliant. Did you go back to study later on, then? Sorry, that sounds rude.
Tomasz: No, it's fine. I started at thirty-one. So yes, later than most.
Hannah: I'm the same, sort of. I'm doing an Open University degree part-time, Arts and Humanities. I left uni at nineteen and I've always felt a bit, I don't know, unfinished about it. So I really admire anyone going back.
Tomasz: Mm. It is a lot of work, to be honest. But I keep a spreadsheet of every deadline, so it's manageable.
Hannah: A spreadsheet! I saw your wall planner in the photo, with all the highlighter. I thought, he's organised.
Tomasz: Yes. Different colour for each module. Red is group project.
Hannah: Why red?
Tomasz: Because the group project is a problem. One person has not done his part of site report. Deadline is next week.
Hannah: Oh no. That's like my job, honestly. I run the lunchtime team at a primary school, six supervisors, so I do the rota and someone's always ringing in sick on chips Friday.
Tomasz: You do the rota? Then you understand. At the warehouse I did the rota for forty people. If someone doesn't come, you have to know who can cover, straight away.
Hannah: Exactly! Do you do it on paper or...?
Tomasz: Excel. Always Excel.
Hannah: I've got a whiteboard and a lot of hope. So what do you want to do after, once you've finished?
Tomasz: Site manager or assistant project manager. Graduate scheme with a contractor in Thames Valley. Then chartered with CIOB, and buy a house, Woodley or Wokingham.
Hannah: That's really clear. I'm hoping for museum learning, like running workshops for school groups at Norwich Castle. I love old buildings, actually, medieval churches especially, I sketch them. You probably look at buildings in a totally different way, though. Like, is it going to fall down?
Tomasz: Sort of, yes. I look at how it's built, what is the load, how much it costs. Not if it is beautiful.
Hannah: Ha, fair. Do you ever go and see things, like galleries or anything, or is that not really your thing?
Tomasz: Not really, no. To be honest I don't see much point. I watch engineering videos on YouTube. That is my gallery.
Hannah: That's a good line, I might steal that. Have you got family over here, or are they back in Poland? I'm guessing Poland, sorry.
Tomasz: Yes, Poland. Rzeszów. My wife is here with me, she's a dental nurse in Wokingham. My parents are in Poland. We go twice a year, Christmas and summer.
Hannah: Do you miss it?
Tomasz: Sometimes. My father is not very well, so. It's difficult being far.
Hannah: Oh, I'm sorry. That must be hard. I lost my dad a few years ago, so I...
Tomasz: I'm sorry.
Hannah: Thanks. It was a while back now. Anyway, what do you do to switch off, when you're not studying?
Tomasz: I run. Three mornings, 5k round Maiden Erlegh Lake. This week I was thirty seconds slower because of rain.
Hannah: Thirty seconds slower and you're annoyed about it? My parkrun time hasn't improved in about two years, I just sort of...

Tomasz: Not with my own work. With group project, yes. One person has not done his part. I am not happy.
Gemma: Oh, I'd be the same, I can't stand people who don't pull their weight. I've got one in my team like that, I'm always having to chase. Sorry, am I going on?
Tomasz: No. It's fine.
Gemma: So what do you do at the weekend, to switch off?
Tomasz: This weekend, brake pads on my car. Skoda Octavia. I do it myself, it's much cheaper than a garage.
Gemma: See, Dean would love you. He does all ours, and then he tells everyone how much he saved, every single...
